newsitem.title: USA: Russia GDP to rise up to 2.5 pct in 1997--Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia GDP to rise up to 2.5 pct in 1997--Chubais.

text.p: Russian Gross Domestic Product should rise between 0.5 percent and a maximum of 2.5 percent this year, Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais told a news conference on Tuesday.
"But if you look at 1998, I think that is the year when you could be surprised," he added.
Chubais said Russian inflation -- an annual 22 percent in 1996 -- was "completely under control." Inflation would not be more than 12 percent in 1997, he said.
He said Russia's economic priorities comprised a realistic budget, new tax policies, radical restructuring of natural monopolies and fighting corruption.
The first steps toward this had already been taken, he said.
